import pandas as pd

# Create the dataframe from the provided table
data = {
    'ngc number': [5408, 5457, 5466, 5474, 5477],
    'object type': ['irregular galaxy', 'spiral galaxy', 'globular cluster', 'spiral galaxy', 'irregular galaxy'],
    'constellation': ['centaurus', 'ursa major', 'boötes', 'ursa major', 'ursa major'],
    'right ascension ( j2000 )': ['14h03 m21.0s', '14h03 m12.5s', '14h05 m27.4s', '14h05 m01.5s', '14h05 m33.1s'],
    'declination ( j2000 )': ['degree22′44″', 'degree20′53″', 'degree32′04″', 'degree39′45″', 'degree27′40″'],
    'apparent magnitude': [14.0, 8.7, 10.5, 11.9, 14.5]
}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Filter for irregular galaxies and spiral galaxies
irregular_df = df[df['object type'] == 'irregular galaxy']
spiral_df = df[df['object type'] == 'spiral galaxy']

# Calculate the mean apparent magnitude for each type
mean_irregular = irregular_df['apparent magnitude'].mean()
mean_spiral = spiral_df['apparent magnitude'].mean()

# Check if the mean of irregular galaxies is exactly 2.1 more than the mean of spiral galaxies
answer = (mean_irregular - mean_spiral) == 2.1
